h1: Press brakes — hydraulic and electric, 22 to 1,323 US tons
intro: A press brake bends sheet and plate between a punch and a V-die; the control sets the back gauge, the ram depth and the angle, and the operator loads the sheet and presses the pedal. NovoTech sells two kinds in Canada, each on its own page: hydraulic press brakes — the lowest price per ton and full force over the whole stroke, from the 33-ton compact and NC machines to CNC brakes of 1,323 US tons and 26 ft, in a premium line made in Turkey and a value line built to our specification — and electric press brakes, servo-driven with no hydraulic oil, 3 to 220 US tons, twice the speed and about 70 % less power for sheet work. A third page covers the horizontal press brakes that bend bar, pipe and busbar. Below, the three kinds compared, every model in one table and the questions we get asked; every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, European-style tooling, a 1-year warranty and installation, training and parts from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: Hydraulic, hybrid or electric — which press brake should I buy?
faq.a: Hydraulic gives the lowest price per ton and full force over the whole stroke — the machine for thick plate, long parts and the widest tonnage range (33 to 1,323 US tons here). A hybrid (the Dener XH) is a hydraulic brake with a servo-driven pump: 42 – 58 % less energy, faster, quieter, for a shop that runs the brake all day. An electric brake (Dener DDM, NovoTech WADG) has no oil at all: ±0.01 mm repeatability, bending speeds to 30 mm/s and about 70 % less power — usually the better buy for 16 ga to 1/4″ sheet in a job shop or a clean environment. Above about 150 tons and on 3/8″ plate, hydraulic still wins. Bar, pipe and busbar are bent on a horizontal press brake, a different machine with its own page.

Both kinds come in two lines, on the same page. The premium line is made in Turkey by Dener on the heaviest frame, with ESA or Delem controls, the longest options list and Dener Canada parts in Mississauga, ON, Canada — the machine for plate and production, two shifts a day. NovoTech's own value line is the same architecture — monoblock frame, Hawe servo valves, linear scales, Delem control — built in China to our specification at about two-thirds of the price: the right buy for a job shop that needs a 100 – 300 ton CNC brake, an electric brake for sheet or an NC brake for repeat parts. The ISITAN compact brakes, 33 – 66 tons over 4 – 7 ft, are for HVAC, enclosures and brackets where a 100-ton machine is more than you need. All are installed and supported by the same NovoTech technicians.

faq.q: How much tonnage and length do I need?
faq.a: Air bending mild steel takes about 575 × t² ÷ V US tons per foot, with the thickness t and the V opening in inches: in the standard V = 8 × thickness die that is about 4 tons per foot for 16 ga, 9 for 1/8″, 13.5 for 3/16″, 18 for 1/4″ and 36 for 1/2″ (29 in a 10 × t die); stainless needs about 50 % more, aluminum about half. Add a foot of length to the longest part you bend and about 20 % headroom. A 10 ft × 1/4″ shop is a 175 – 220 ton machine; 10 ft × 3/8″ a 250 – 320 ton machine; 13 ft × 1/2″, bent in a 5 – 6″ V, a 400 – 450 ton machine. Tell us your thickest and longest bend and we size the brake and the tooling.

An NC brake positions the back gauge and the ram depth from a stored program, with the two cylinders kept in step by a torsion bar — rigid, cheap to maintain, right for the same parts in one material every day. A CNC brake measures the ram on linear scales and corrects it through servo valves, calculates the bend from the drawing, crowns the bed and changes material in the program — the machine for mixed work, tight angles and multi-bend parts. NovoTech's value line has both; Dener and ISITAN CNC brakes come with 2D or 3D graphic controls.

faq.q: What tooling fits, and do you stock it?
faq.a: European-style (Promecam / Amada) segmented punches and dies with quick-release clamping are standard on every line, and a sectioned punch set with a 2-V die ships with each machine. NovoTech stocks Eurostamp press brake tooling in Canada — punches, dies, radius, hemming and joggle tools, gooseneck and special profiles — and sizes it to your machine; Wila hydraulic clamping and American-style adapters are options.

faq.q: What about safety and the Ontario pre-start review?
faq.a: Side guards, an enclosed rear guard, interlocked doors and an anti-panic foot pedal with emergency stop are standard; DSP or Fiessler laser finger protection and light curtains are options we recommend for every CNC machine. In Ontario a new press brake needs a pre-start health and safety review (PSR) under Regulation 851 before it runs; NovoTech prepares the documentation for it.

faq.q: Do you deliver, install and service in Canada?
faq.a: Yes — every press brake is shipped to Mississauga, ON, Canada, unloaded, levelled, commissioned and the operators trained by NovoTech; Dener Canada and NovoTech stock the parts here. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, 600 V standard (208 / 240 / 480 V on request), a 1-year warranty and remote diagnostics through the control.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
